source_locators: The assessment defines Tongass old-growth sawtimber as over 150 years old while noting that the full complement of old-growth features may not occur until about 250 years.
It reports 405,000 acres of productive old growth harvested from 1954–1995 and estimates another 45,000 acres from 1909–1954, for 450,000 acres total.
The assessment reports about 5.6 million acres of productive forest and states that clearcut even-aged management was the predominant harvest method.
GAO states that the Tongass timber program had been based on harvesting old-growth trees since the early twentieth century and that the transition to young growth was announced in 2010.
Forest Service data reviewed by GAO show average annual timber-related expenditures of $12.5 million and revenues of $1.1 million from fiscal years 2005–2014.
The expenditure figure excludes road construction and maintenance; the receipt therefore does not add an estimated road cost.

transformations.formula: Normalize the Forest Service estimate of 450,000 productive old-growth acres harvested, preserving the inventory-based and volume-derived portions separately.
Calculate $12.5 million average annual expenditures - $1.1 million average annual revenues = $11.4 million from FY2005–2014; do not add unreported road costs.
Calculate 1995 - 1909 = 86 years for the cumulative old-growth harvest assessment.
Calculate 450,000 / 5,600,000 × 100 = 8.035714 percent within the Tongass productive-forest boundary.
0.35B + 0.30H + 0.20P + 0.15E; convert to 1-10 with 1 + 9 × composite and round to one decimal.

receipts.uncertainty: The 45,000-acre 1909–1954 quantity is estimated from reported saw-log volume and an assumed per-acre harvest volume, while the 405,000-acre 1954–1995 quantity is inventory-based. Productive forest is a timber-capability class and is not identical to the old-growth denominator in every ecological interpretation. The 2005–2014 fiscal figures cover the Tongass timber program during a period when GAO describes the program as historically old-growth-based, but the figures are not allocated sale-by-sale between old and young growth. Net public cost excludes road construction and maintenance and is an administrative fiscal burden, not an ecological valuation.
receipts.freshness: Cumulative 1909–1995 harvest assessment and FY2005–2014 program accounts reviewed 2026-08-01T00:00:00.000Z.

selection_reason.selected_method_passed: Forest Service and GAO records provide an explicit old-growth definition, accumulated harvest area, duration, productive-forest extent and realized timber-program expenditure and revenue burden.
higher_priority_failures: The evidence is a named U.S. national forest rather than a defensible global current aggregation.
No globally comparable annual old-growth-harvest series with a stable old-growth definition and at least 20 complete years is available for the current-data method.
